HEADLINE: Saudi air defences intercept Houthi barrage near Mecca

THIS IS AN ADVANCE ON THE 08:22 EDITION, NOT A REPEAT. This morning we ran the Riyadh interception and the airport reopening. New tonight: interceptions over MECCA PROVINCE, a GCC condemnation framed around the holy sites, and a full interception tally.

HARD FIGURES — ALL ATTRIBUTED
- Saudi Civil Defence said shrapnel from TWO intercepted ballistic missiles, suspected to have been fired by Yemen's Houthi rebels, fell in Jeddah, Taif, Rabigh and Wadi Al-Mughammas, in MECCA PROVINCE. (Saudi Civil Defence is the asserting party.)
- A drone AND a ballistic missile were intercepted over Riyadh during the same barrage, "which began Saturday evening".
- By midday Sunday, coalition forces had intercepted a cruise missile targeting Khamis Mushait, with warning sirens sounding across Taif and Jazan.
- "In total, 10 ballistic missiles directed at the southern region were intercepted."
- RUNNING TOTAL IF YOU ADD THEM UP: 2 ballistic (Mecca province) + 1 drone and 1 ballistic (Riyadh) + 1 cruise (Khamis Mushait) + 10 ballistic (southern region) = 15 projectiles. AL JAZEERA DOES NOT PRINT A TOTAL OF 15. If you use that number, say it is the sum of the figures Al Jazeera gives, or use the components instead. The number LAUNCHED is nowhere stated — only the number intercepted.
- The photo caption reads: "Saudi authorities examine fragments of two ballistic missiles fired by the Houthis towards Mecca and Medina [SPA]". NOTE: the caption says Mecca AND MEDINA; the article body says Mecca province only and never mentions Medina. CONFLICT WITHIN THE SAME PAGE. Do not write "Medina" on the strength of a photo caption.

NAMED QUOTES WITH EXACT ROLES
- Jasem Mohamed AlBudaiwi, Secretary-General of the Gulf Cooperation Council: the strikes represented "a grave violation of the sanctity of the Holy Sites and a provocation to the sentiments of Muslims worldwide", referring to the interceptions in Mecca, home of the Kaaba and Masjid al-Haram.
- Yahya Saree, Houthi military spokesman, early Sunday, warning civilians away from Riyadh's airport: "King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh is not safe because it is a military target, and we renew our warning to airlines, employees, and travelers." THIS QUOTE RAN IN THE 08:22 EDITION. Do not run it again as new.
- Saree also announced SEVEN operations targeting Saudi oil facilities and military bases. HOUTHI ASSERTION, uncorroborated.
- "The Houthis, a Zaydi Shia group, have denied targeting Muslim holy sites in Saudi Arabia." HOUTHI DENIAL — carry it if you carry AlBudaiwi.

AIRPORT — SMALL ADVANCE ON THIS MORNING
- "Riyadh announced late Saturday that international flights from King Khalid International Airport would resume from Terminal 2 on Sunday, while Terminal 1 would be designated for domestic flights." The terminal split is new detail.
- Context: flights were suspended after waves of Houthi strikes "including one on October 10 that killed 13 people and wounded hundreds".

YEMEN GROUND WAR — ONE SIDE'S CLAIM ONLY
- "On Sunday, Yemen's armed forces said the military had carried out 736 strikes on Houthi positions over the past 24 hours, leading to 307 people being 'neutralised' and the destruction of 68 military vehicles." THIS IS THE INTERNATIONALLY RECOGNISED GOVERNMENT'S CLAIM, uncorroborated, and "neutralised" is their word. Label it as their assertion or omit.
- Forces aligned with the internationally recognised government launched "Operation Dawn of Yemen" on 5 October to retake lost territory. The Houthis captured Yemen's western coast including Mocha in a September offensive.

HUMANITARIAN — NON-APPROVED ORIGINATING BODY
- The Rasd Organization for Rights and Freedoms warned on Taiz: "About 1,110 kidney failure patients face the risks of a shortage of dialysis supplies, given the need for about 120 dialysis sessions daily along with 192 patients in intensive care units and 154 children in incubators, due to the Houthi siege imposed on the city of Taiz since October 4."
- Rasd is NOT an approved source. Al Jazeera is the approved source reporting it. Attribute to Al Jazeera reporting Rasd, or omit.

SECOND APPROVED SOURCE FOR THE CENTRAL CLAIM: PARTIAL ONLY. Al Jazeera's own companion piece "Saudi Arabia intercepts missiles and drones as fighting with Houthis rages" (same outlet, so not independent) reports two injuries in Saudi Arabia's south. CNN world index at 17:42 GMT carried "UK to deploy fighter jets to defend Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks" but I did not open or date it. I found NO non-Al-Jazeera approved source for the Mecca-province interceptions. TREAT THE MECCA ANGLE AS SINGLE-SOURCED.
